deployment.name: Publix Atlanta Marathon 2027
deployment.description: Marathon, half marathon and 5K through downtown Atlanta on Sunday 7 March 2027. ARES puts a radio operator at every aid station, in each SAG vehicle, with the pace, cone and course-director vehicles, at the medical tent, and staffs net control in the AFCEMA MACC. Two voice nets (RACE and SAG) plus APRS-IS tracking of vehicles.
deployment.tasking_reference: ATC volunteer radio operator request, January 2027

positions.name: ARES command (IC and Ops Chief)
positions.briefing_notes: Incident commander and operations chief for the ARES element. Liaison with ATC and AFCEMA in the room. The IC does not run a net.

positions.name: Net control, RACE net
positions.briefing_notes: Two operators: NCO on the radio, assistant tracking aid-station traffic and relaying to the room. Runner-needs-assistance and runner-down traffic comes to you first; hand SAG dispatch to NCS SAG.

positions.name: Net control, SAG net
positions.briefing_notes: NCO plus assistant. Dispatch SAGs and motos by pickup location (NOVEMBER, SIERRA, ECHO, WHISKEY points on the ARES map). Track every dispatched pickup until the runner is delivered.

positions.name: APRS tracking desk
positions.briefing_notes: Watch vehicle positions on aprs.fi, flag any vehicle not beaconing, and send dispatch details to SAGs by APRS message when the SAG net is busy.

positions.name: Phone desk
positions.briefing_notes: Answer the ARES all-call line, take messages for the nets, call motos and drivers without radios. No amateur licence required.

positions.name: AID MILE 2
positions.briefing_notes: Shadow the station captain. Keep the AID Station SAG Request Log; photograph it for net control after the event. Three messages cover most of the day: "Runner needs assistance at AID MILE 2", "Runner down at AID MILE 2, bib number, injury", and "AID MILE 2 closing".

safety_checklist.template_name: ARRL Field Day safety check list

items.text: Fuel for generators stored properly and safely away from operating positions
Fire extinguisher on hand and readily available at each generator and operating position
First aid kit on hand and its location known to everyone on site
Access to NWS or other weather information; a plan for severe weather
Tent stakes, guy lines and cables flagged; trip hazards marked or covered
Electrical wiring safe: GFCI protection, properly rated extension cords, no exposed connections
Generators properly grounded; exhaust away from people, tents and openings
All antenna supports and towers erected with adequate help and clear of power lines
Antenna structures, masts and guys checked before use and after weather changes
RF exposure evaluated; feedlines and antennas kept out of reach where power justifies it
Fuel, gas cylinders and generators kept away from open flames and smoking
Site access and lighting adequate for arrivals and departures after dark
Adequate water, shade and rest arrangements for the expected weather
Minors supervised by an adult at all times; visitors briefed on hazards
Emergency contacts, nearest hospital and site address posted at the operating positions
Safety briefing delivered to every operator on arrival
